7.4 Indicator Definitions and Measurement Notes

(a) For PI-01, a "beneficiary reached" is defined as any individual who participates in a structured outreach activity, including health talks, screening sessions, or mobile clinic visits. An individual attending multiple sessions shall be counted only once per quarter for reporting purposes. The cumulative target of 25,000 beneficiaries shall be tracked on a rolling basis from the Effective Date.

(b) For PI-02, a "community health talk" is defined as a structured educational session lasting at least 45 minutes, delivered by a trained health educator or community health worker, to a group of at least 15 participants. Sessions conducted as part of school visits, market sensitisation, or religious gathering outreach shall all be counted.

(c) For PI-03, a "community health worker trained" refers to an individual who completes the full training curriculum and passes the post-training assessment. Refresher training for previously trained workers shall not be counted as new training for the purpose of this indicator.

(d) For PI-04, a "referral" is defined as a documented case where a beneficiary is directed to a formal health facility for further assessment or treatment. Referrals must be recorded in the standard referral logbook and accompanied by a referral slip.

documents.content:
I write to convey the approval of the Kano State Primary Health Care Management Board for the conduct of the proposed community health outreach campaign in the above-named Local Government Areas. The approval date for the campaign is recorded as 10th March, 2025, and this letter serves as the official authorisation for all preparatory activities to commence forthwith.

The Board, at its meeting held on 6th March, 2025, considered your request dated 24th February, 2025, alongside the submitted workplan, budget estimates, and the technical review comments from the State Epidemiologist. After due deliberation, the Board resolved to approve the campaign subject to the following conditions:

1. The campaign shall be conducted within the approved budget ceiling of ₦38,500,000 (Thirty-Eight Million, Five Hundred Thousand Naira Only), as detailed in the attached budget schedule. Any variation exceeding 10% of this ceiling shall require fresh approval from the Board.

2. All community health extension workers (CHEWs), volunteer community mobilisers, and other personnel engaged for the campaign shall be drawn from the State's verified personnel register. The Board reserves the right to audit the personnel list at any time.

3. The campaign shall prioritise the following interventions:
   - Routine immunisation catch-up for children under five (measles, pentavalent, and polio vaccines)
   - Distribution of insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) and long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) to households
   - Health education sessions on maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) practices
   - Screening for hypertension and diabetes among adults aged 40 years and above
   - Referral of identified cases to secondary health facilities

4. The approved campaign shall run for a period of fourteen (14) working days, commencing on 24th March, 2025, and concluding on 11th April, 2025. Any extension of this timeline must be justified in writing and submitted for consideration at least one week before the scheduled conclusion date.

The approval letter from Kano State Primary Health Care Management Board records approval_date_for_campaign as 2025-03-10. Record status: current.

5. The Board's Monitoring and Evaluation Unit shall conduct spot checks during the campaign. All field teams must cooperate fully with the monitoring officers and provide access to records, registers, and logistics documentation upon request.

6. A comprehensive end-of-campaign report shall be submitted to the Board within two weeks of campaign conclusion. The report shall include, but not be limited to: the number of individuals reached by each intervention, vaccination coverage data, and a financial expenditure statement certified by the Internal Audit Unit.

7. All outreach activities shall be conducted in compliance with the State's health safety protocols and the National Health Act, 2014. The campaign shall not disrupt the routine services at primary health care centres within the designated LGAs.

8. The Board acknowledges that the campaign will utilise the existing cold chain storage facilities at Rikados, Gwale, and Tarauni PHC centres. The State Cold Chain Officer has confirmed that the facilities are functional and have adequate capacity for the vaccines and other temperature-sensitive commodities.

Please note that this approval is specific to Round 4 of the community health outreach campaign as described in your submission. It does not constitute a blanket approval for subsequent rounds or for activities outside the scope of the submitted workplan.
